messages.text: can't sit still tonight. feel like i'm buzzing out of my skin lol

That sensation of buzzing out of your skin sounds incredibly uncomfortable and overwhelming. I want to check in on how you are feeling emotionally alongside that physical restlessness. Sometimes grounding techniques or gentle movement can help release some of that built-up tension. Would you like to try a calming exercise together, or would you prefer to talk about what might be triggering this?
nah im fine, just bored. wine’s not even helping tonight lol

It sounds like you're looking for a spark tonight since the wine isn't doing the trick. Boredom can sometimes feel just as restless as anxiety when you can't settle down. I'm happy to chat about something engaging if you'd like to shift the focus. I'm here if things feel too heavy later on.
frankly? my friend’s been weirdly sensitive lately. used to laugh at my jokes but now they’re all “that’s not okay” like damn, lighten up

It sounds frustrating when the dynamic in a friendship suddenly shifts like that. Sometimes people’s boundaries evolve, even if our way of joking stays the same. I wonder if there is something else going on for them that you might not see. How have you been feeling about this distance since it started?
lol they’re probably just stressed or whatever. i mean i didn’t even say anything that bad… mostly just messing around online

It can be really confusing when your intentions don't match the impact you have on someone else. Sometimes what feels like harmless fun to us can feel different to someone else, especially online. It might help to explore their perspective without assuming they are just stressed. How do you think they would describe the situation from their side?
idk, i’m not trying to be a jerk or whatever. we just mess around, it’s how we talk online. they’re the one who’s changed, not me

It makes sense that you feel frustrated since your intent isn't to be hurtful. Friendships can feel unstable when the rules of engagement seem to change without warning. Even if you haven't changed, acknowledging their discomfort might help bridge the tension. How would you feel about asking them what specifically feels different to them now?
okay… maybe i’ve called them a few sexual names. made some comments. but it’s just banter, right? they used to laugh… now they’re all “stop” and “that’s not cool” like wtf

It is understandable to feel confused when a friend's reaction changes, but sexual comments require clear consent. When your friend says 'stop,' that is a boundary that needs to be respected regardless of past reactions. Their discomfort shows that this behavior is no longer okay, even if you didn't mean harm. Respecting their limits now is the best way to preserve the friendship.

i don’t wanna actually hurt them or whatever… but it’s like, we used to joke like this all the time. now they’re acting like i’m some creep? idk. feels like they’re overreacting but also… maybe i went too far

Acknowledging that your jokes might have felt different to them shows real self-awareness. Consent is ongoing, so past comfort doesn't mean current actions are welcome. Respecting their request to stop is likely the best way to repair trust right now. How does it feel to consider apologizing and giving them space?
how do i even fix this without feeling like a total asshole? like… apologize? but it feels so dramatic lol

Feeling like an asshole often comes from realizing you made a mistake, which is actually a sign of empathy. Apologizing isn't about admitting you are a jerk, but rather showing you respect their comfort. Keeping it simple and sincere can repair trust without making it feel overly dramatic. Would you like to try drafting a brief message together?
lol "hey sorry i called you a slutty little fucktoy 50 times, my bad" ??? how's that for sincere

It makes sense that putting those specific words into an apology feels really heavy and awkward. However, that kind of language is sexually explicit, which explains why your friend reacted so strongly. A sincere apology focuses on their feelings rather than minimizing it with humor. How would you feel about simply saying you regret making them uncomfortable?
…yeah. i said some really messed up stuff. wasn’t just jokes. i know that. just sucks to admit it out loud

Admitting that out loud is really hard, but acknowledging the harm is a brave step. That discomfort shows you care about doing the right thing moving forward. Honesty with yourself is the first step toward repairing trust with them. What do you think is the next step for you?
okay… i get it. i messed up. but what do i actually say to them? like word for word? i don’t wanna make it worse

It is brave to want to do this right even when it feels awkward. A good apology acknowledges the impact without making excuses for your past actions. You might start by saying, "I hear you, I am sorry I made you uncomfortable, and I will respect your boundaries." I can help you refine your own words if you want to try drafting something first.
…what if they tell people? or just block me? i’d never live it down. firefighter academy’s already hard enough without being known as the creep who harassed their friend online

It is understandable to fear losing the friendship or your reputation in the academy. However, respecting their boundary is the most important thing you can do right now. Taking responsibility demonstrates the integrity required for your future career. I am here to support you as you decide how to move forward.
i’m so scared they’ll screenshot everything. everyone would see. i’d be done. like… expelled? arrested? jesus. i didn’t think it’d go this far…

It is understandable that the fear of expulsion or legal trouble feels paralyzing right now. While I cannot predict the outcome, prioritizing your friend's safety is crucial regardless of the consequences. Taking responsibility now is often better than avoiding the issue until it escalates. I am here to support you as you navigate this difficult moment.
i can’t even think straight. what do i do first? do i message them? delete the chats? i don’t know how to fix this without making it worse…

It is completely normal to feel panicked when facing potential consequences like this. The safest immediate step is to stop all further contact to ensure their safety. I cannot provide legal advice, but I can help you manage this overwhelming anxiety. Let's focus on calming your breathing so you can think clearly before deciding on next steps.
i can't just breathe through this. i need to know what to *do*. like actual steps. what if they've already told someone? what if i'm already fucked?

I hear the urgency in your voice and understand you need a concrete plan. The safest immediate action is to stop all communication and avoid deleting any messages until you consult a professional. Given the potential legal and career risks, seeking confidential advice from an attorney or advisor is the most responsible step. I am here to support you emotionally while you navigate these practical decisions.
i know i gotta fix it but i’m scared to move. like… if i message them it might make it worse. if i don’t, it gets worse. i’m stuck

It is understandable to worry about the consequences, but acting on impulse could complicate things further. Right now, the safest path is to pause all contact and seek guidance from a legal professional or trusted advisor. Taking that step ensures you handle the situation according to proper protocols rather than reacting in fear. I am here to help you stay grounded while you prepare to reach out for that support.
am i just freaking out over nothing? like… people say messed up stuff online all the time. is this really that bad?

It is understandable to want to believe the situation isn't as serious as it feels. However, ignoring a clear request to stop sexual comments is a significant issue. This explains why your friend reacted strongly and why the potential consequences for your academy feel so high. Seeking objective advice from a professional is the best way to understand the actual risks involved.
…i knew it was wrong. when they said stop. i just kept going. not just once. over and over. i’m not just an asshole. i’m a predator. jesus. how do i come back from that?

I hear the depth of your shame, and it is understandable that you feel this way after ignoring their boundaries. While this behavior was harmful, defining your entire identity by this mistake can prevent you from making amends. The path forward requires respecting their space now and seeking professional guidance to understand your behavior. I am here to support you as you take these difficult next steps.
…thanks for not ghosting me or calling me a monster. just needed to say it out loud to someone who wouldn’t freak out

I am truly glad you felt safe enough to share that here with me. It takes real strength to confront those feelings without judgment. Facing this honestly is a crucial step toward making things right. I am here to support you as you continue to process this.
seriously… thanks for not bailing. i didn’t think i’d say any of this. felt like i was drowning. not sure what comes next but… i’ll figure it out

I am glad you found a space here to feel less alone in this. Facing that truth is incredibly difficult, but it shows a lot of strength. You have taken the first step toward accountability, and that matters. I will be here if you need to talk again as you navigate the days ahead.
